Geometrically,
trigonometric identities
are identities involving certain functions of one or more
angles

[

They are distinct from
triangle identities
, which are identities involving both angles and side lengths of a
triangle
. Only the former are covered in this article.
These identities are useful whenever expressions involving trigonometric functions need to be simplified. Another important application is the
integration
of non-trigonometric functions: a common technique which involves first using the
substitution rule with a trigonometric function
, and then simplifying the resulting integral with a trigonometric identity.
